title: Rencontre dans le couloir  (Meeting in the Hallway)

segments.t: Stepping out into the hallway of ASK, Sofia and Gabriel accompany Julien Dore. When Mathias hands Sofia an administrative errand in front of Julien, she quickly covers for herself, while the agency's new owner Hicham makes a lively impression. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Il a une drôle de façon de traiter les acteurs.
C'est juste une blague pour une pièce.
Mathias rigole toujours avec tout le monde!
Hicham Janowski arrive dans le couloir.
C'est le nouveau propriétaire de l'agence?
Oui, mais il s'occupe de la comptabilité.
Qui est cette femme magnifique là-bas?
C'est le mannequin Aymeline Val.
Elle veut aussi devenir actrice?
Oui, Andréa s'occupe de sa carrière.
Vous avez une agence formidable!
Merci pour cette belle rencontre, Julien.
Au revoir, à très bientôt pour répéter!
Let's examine the conversation in the hallway line by line.
Il a une drôle de façon de traiter les acteurs.
'He has a strange way of treating actors.' Put ahead of 'way' with 'of', the word that usually means 'funny' shifts to mean 'strange' or 'odd' in French.
C'est juste une blague pour une pièce.
'It is just a joke for a play.' At the end, what looks like English 'piece' is short for 'theater piece' and means a stage 'play' in French.
Mathias rigole toujours avec tout le monde!
'Mathias is always joking around with everyone!' Julien chooses an informal everyday action that means 'laughs' or 'jokes around', placing 'always' right after it rather than before.
Hicham Janowski arrive dans le couloir.
'Hicham Janowski arrives in the hallway.' Simple present 'arrives' covers 'is arriving right now' in French, paired with 'in the corridor' at the end.
C'est le nouveau propriétaire de l'agence?
'He is the new owner of the agency?' Introducing a person with a role takes 'it is' rather than 'he is' in French, followed by a cognate of 'proprietor' meaning 'owner'.
Oui, mais il s'occupe de la comptabilité.
'Yes, but he takes care of accounting.' Built from 'occupies himself of', this handy expression means 'deals with' or 'runs', followed by 'accounting'.
Qui est cette femme magnifique là-bas?
'Who is that gorgeous woman over there?' Linking 'there' and 'low' with a hyphen at the end builds 'over there' in French, while 'magnificent' follows 'woman'.
C'est le mannequin Aymeline Val.
'That is the model Aymeline Val.' Curiously in French, this job title meaning 'fashion model' keeps 'the' in its male form even when referring to Aymeline.
Elle veut aussi devenir actrice?
'Does she also want to become an actress?' Sliding 'also' between 'wants' and 'to become' is natural in French, and 'actress' stands bare without 'an'.
Oui, Andréa s'occupe de sa carrière.
'Yes, Andrea is managing her career.' Notice how 'her' in French takes the '-a' form to match 'career', rather than matching the person who owns it.
Vous avez une agence formidable!
'You have a wonderful agency!' Unlike English 'formidable', which can sound intimidating, this cognate in French is pure praise meaning 'wonderful' or 'terrific'.
Merci pour cette belle rencontre, Julien.
'Thank you for this lovely meeting, Julien.' Before 'encounter', 'beautiful' softens in sense to 'lovely', giving you a warm thank-you expression in French.
Au revoir, à très bientôt pour répéter!

'Goodbye, see you very soon to rehearse!' Watch the theater false friend at the end: what looks like 'repeat' means 'rehearse' in French, right after 'until very soon'. Now let's listen to the whole scene once more from start to finish.

Sofia skillfully manages the awkward encounter in the hallway, while Julien leaves with high spirits and an eagerness to collaborate on his musical soundtrack. Let's review the conversational phrases and vocabulary from this scene. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
